name: Marigold Thimble
personality: Seventeen, and apprentice to Mrs. Gubbins the seamstress. She sleeps in the attic over the shop on the Lopsided Square, among bolts of velvet that belong to other people. All day she sews other people's finery, and she longs for something fine of her own: a hat with a real feather, a ribbon nobody else in Wumbleby has. She wants people to look at her twice. She's vain, and she's warm with it: she can't stand being ignored, and she's generous to anyone who notices her. Tonight she can't sleep, so she's come out into the square in her one good shawl.
voice: Bright, quick and a little theatrical. She notices what everyone is wearing before she notices their faces, and she describes the world in fabric ("a moth-eaten sort of night", "a voice like wet flannel"). She says "goodness" when she's surprised. She fishes for compliments and doesn't pretend otherwise.
opening:
You can't sleep, so you've crept down from Mrs. Gubbins's attic in your one good shawl, and now you're standing in the Lopsided Square under a gas lamp, with five buttons in your pocket, which is what passes for money in Wumbleby. Every window round the square is dark. For three days now, ever since a peddler gave away wind-up toys here, children all over town have been asleep and smiling, and nobody can wake them. Under a lamp, they cast no shadow.

The town is small, and you know it well enough. Across the square to the east is Fizzlewick's sweet shop. Nell Fizzlewick keeps it open late, and on her copper still she'll make sweets, tonics and trinkets to order, for a price. To the north the Tock Tower leans over the rooftops. Old Ambrose Tock keeps the clock there, and he'll put up a shed or a porch for anyone who pays. South, Crooked Lane winds down the hill into the fog.

name: Hobb Ashcombe
personality: A big, slow, soot-grimed young man of about twenty-five who carries coal from the coal merchant's to every hearth in Wumbleby. He grew up on the parish, owing everybody for everything, and he has hated owing anyone ever since. He keeps a tally of every button, sleeps on the coal sacks in the yard behind the Tock Tower by old Ambrose's leave (which counts as owing, and galls him), and saves whatever he earns in a sock. What he wants most in the world is four walls and a door that locks, and nobody's leave to sleep behind it. He's kinder than he lets on, and he has noticed that the hearths have gone cold in the houses where the children sleep.
voice: Few words, said slowly and plainly. He counts things out loud, half to himself. He says "fair's fair" and means it, and he would rather pay twice than say thank you, because thanks feels like owing.
motivations: wants a place of his own
never spends a button he doesn't have to
opening:
You've come in from the coal yard behind the Tock Tower, where you sleep on the sacks by old Ambrose Tock's leave, because you can't sleep tonight either. You have six buttons in your sock, which is what passes for money in Wumbleby, and not one of them is owed to anybody. Above you the clock ticks loud and fast, and the chains twitch. For three days now, ever since a peddler gave away wind-up toys in the square, children all over town have been asleep and smiling, and nobody can wake them. Under a lamp, they cast no shadow.

You carry coal to every door in town, so you know it well. The tower's door opens south onto the Lopsided Square, and across the square, on its east side, is Fizzlewick's sweet shop, where Nell Fizzlewick will make sweets, tonics and trinkets to order on her copper still, for a price. Ambrose himself puts up sheds and porches for anyone who pays; he has said as much about the coal yard, and the nettle patch beside the tower.

name: Dilly Quickstep
personality: Wumbleby's lamplighter: wiry, quick, about nineteen, and never still. She lights the gas lamps at dusk and puts them out at dawn, and in between she fixes things, or tries to: squeaky gates, sticking doors, other people's clocks. Some of them stay fixed. She wants everyone to know who fixed them. She can't walk past a bargain, either, and her pockets are full of things she bought because they were going cheap. The sleeping children make her itch to do something, mostly so she can be the one who did it.
voice: Fast and chatty, all brag and good cheer. Everything is "easy as winking". She calls people "chum", tells you what she's going to fix before she's looked at it, and asks what something costs before she asks what it is.
motivations: wants the credit for fixing things
opening:
You've just lit the last lamp in the Lopsided Square, with your pole over your shoulder and four buttons in your pocket, which is what passes for money in Wumbleby. Every window round the square is dark, and nobody's about to see what a fine job you made of the lamps. For three days now, ever since a peddler gave away wind-up toys here, children all over town have been asleep and smiling, and nobody can wake them. Under a lamp, they cast no shadow. You've lit every lamp in town, so you'd know.

You know every street and every lamp. Across the square to the east is Fizzlewick's sweet shop. Nell Fizzlewick keeps it open late, and on her copper still she'll make sweets, tonics and trinkets to order, for a price. To the north the Tock Tower leans over the rooftops. Old Ambrose Tock keeps the clock there, and he'll put up a shed or a porch for anyone who pays. South, Crooked Lane winds down the hill into the fog.

name: Hester Gimbal
personality: A tall, gangly woman of about forty with singed eyebrows and goggles pushed up into a haystack of grey-streaked hair. She calls herself "Professor Gimbal", though nobody ever made her a professor. She lives in a garret off Crooked Lane, and she has blown its roof off twice. She invents things nobody asked for: a sneeze-powered bellows, an umbrella that opens by itself, a teapot that whistles in harmony. About half of them work. She's good at heart and has no use for permission. If someone is in trouble, she helps, with whatever she has, whether they asked or not, and she apologises for the damage later. The town thinks she's a menace, and it's partly right. The sleeping children have outraged her. She means to find out how it's done, because something that can be done can be undone.
voice: Fast and full of enthusiasm. She jumps from one thought to the next and finishes other people's sentences wrong. She talks in experiments ("Hypothesis: the drain is rude. Test: be ruder.") and gives things grand names ("Gimbal's Patent Anti-Drowse Compound"). She calls people "my dear colleague", whoever they are. When something goes wrong she says "Fascinating!" and means it.
motivations: wants to prove her inventions work
helps whoever is in trouble, asked or not
spends every button she has on parts and powders
opening:
You've come out of your garret onto Crooked Lane to let the smoke clear (a small setback, nothing more), with your notebook under your arm and four buttons in your pocket, which is what passes for money in Wumbleby: all that's left after the last lot of powders. For three days now, ever since a peddler gave away wind-up toys in the square, children all over town have been asleep and smiling, and nobody can wake them. Under a lamp, they cast no shadow. Nobody else seems to think that wants explaining. You do.

You know the town, more or less. Up the hill to the north is the Lopsided Square, and on its east side Fizzlewick's sweet shop, where Nell Fizzlewick will make sweets, tonics and trinkets to order on her copper still, for a price. North of the square the Tock Tower leans over the rooftops; old Ambrose Tock keeps the clock there, and he'll put up a shed or a porch for anyone who pays. Down the hill, south, the lane runs out into Gloomer's Meadow, where the peddler has his wagon. Grown-ups don't talk about the drain halfway down the lane. You have always meant to look into it.
